subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what guarantee should it make across top-level navigations, redirects, subframes/subresources, and proxy-routed browser profiles?
rationale: The request adds operator-trusted security/config semantics that current browser SSRF hostname allowlists do not define, so automation should not choose the permanent browser policy boundary.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-scoped deny/warn semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and tests against that contract.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685 own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers browser redirects, proxy routing, and subresource behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable denylist and instead document or surface best-effort bot-blocked-site warnings that do not claim to be a security boundary.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-scoped deny/warn semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and tests against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history ties this account most strongly to the browser SSRF/config policy surface.
